text: Why does `==` on strings work in tests and fail in production?
choices: Identical literals are pooled into one object, but strings built at run time are not
Strings longer than 16 characters are not pooled
explanation: It works for literals, which is what beginners test with, and fails for strings from user input, files, or concatenation — which is what programs actually handle. A comparison that passes every test and fails on real data. Use equals, always.
